prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection in the StreamableHTTP client ultimately fails (max reconnection attempts exceeded / reconnection error), the client previously just logged and returned, leaving the original caller's pending request awaiting a response that will never arrive — an indefinite hang. Both PRs modify the reconnection-failure path in _handle_reconnection to surface that failure to the caller instead of silently swallowing it. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection in the StreamableHTTP client ultimately fails (max reconnection attempts exceeded / reconnection error), the client previously just logged and returned, leaving the original caller's pending request awaiting a response that will never arrive — an indefinite hang. Both PRs modify the reconnection-failure path in _handle_reconnection to surface that failure to the caller instead of silently swallowing it. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2395 is the smaller, more surgical fix: it stays inside _handle_reconnection and synthesizes a JSONRPCError keyed to the specific pending request id (via ctx.session_message), which fits the existing JSON-RPC request/response correlation model and only fails the one in-flight request. It also removes the pre-existing '# pragma: no cover' on the exceeded-attempts branch and adds a deliberate '# pragma: no branch' marker, indicating a new test now exercises this path. #3098 instead introduces a recursive _unwrap_exception helper to pull a StreamableHTTPError out of anyio ExceptionGroups and raises an exception from the reconnection path — a more invasive change (tears down via exception propagation rather than a scoped JSON-RPC error) whose diff shows no equivalent test-coverage signal, and it directly conflicts with #2395 since both rewrite the same 'attempt >= MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS' branch with incompatible error-surfacing strategies.

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: func_metadata.py's pre_parse_json() calls json.loads() on any string argument whose field annotation isn't exactly `str`, which corrupts legitimate string values that happen to parse as JSON (e.g. "123", "[1,2]", "null") when the field type is a union like `str | None` or `str | list[str]`. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: func_metadata.py's pre_parse_json() calls json.loads() on any string argument whose field annotation isn't exactly `str`, which corrupts legitimate string values that happen to parse as JSON (e.g. "123", "[1,2]", "null") when the field type is a union like `str | None` or `str | list[str]`. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs add a helper to gate pre-parsing based on the union's members, but #2032's _should_pre_parse_json() skips parsing for ANY union composed only of {str,int,float,bool,NoneType} (e.g. also changes behavior for str|int, str|bool, not just the reported str|None corruption case), and it checks raw union args against a type frozenset without unwrapping Annotated — so a field typed `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` is NOT recognized as optional-str (the Annotated object is never in _SIMPLE_TYPES) and still hits the original corruption bug. #3056 adds _unwrap_annotated() specifically to strip Annotated before the optional-str check, so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` is correctly handled, and it scopes the fix precisely to the reported str|None case rather than silently changing parsing semantics for other simple-type unions.

prs.title: fix(client/auth): discover AS metadata before cold-start token refresh, with issuer-binding check
prs.author: app/claude
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a process restart with only a stored refresh token, no OAuth authorization-server metadata is available in memory, so a cold-start token refresh has no token endpoint to call and either fails or forces re-discovery/re-authorization. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a process restart with only a stored refresh token, no OAuth authorization-server metadata is available in memory, so a cold-start token refresh has no token endpoint to call and either fails or forces re-discovery/re-authorization. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3263 fixes cold-start refresh without changing any public interfaces: it adds an in-memory `eager_discovery_attempted` flag on `OAuthContext` and performs discovery before the refresh call, so it works for every existing `TokenStorage` implementation immediately. It also adds an issuer-binding check on the discovered metadata, a security validation absent from the other approach. #2492 instead extends the `TokenStorage` Protocol with new `get_oauth_metadata`/`set_oauth_metadata` methods that default to a no-op, meaning the fix only takes effect once every downstream storage implementation is updated to persist metadata, and it re-uses persisted metadata across restarts with no re-validation against the current issuer.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs add a helper to gate pre-parsing based on the union's members, but #2032's _should_pre_parse_json() skips parsing for ANY union composed only of {str,int,float,bool,NoneType} (e.g. also changes behavior for str|int, str|bool, not just the reported str|None corruption case), and it checks raw union args against a type frozenset without unwrapping Annotated — so a field typed `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` is NOT recognized as optional-str (the Annotated object is never in _SIMPLE_TYPES) and still hits the original corruption bug. #3056 adds _unwrap_annotated() specifically to strip Annotated before the optional-str check, so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` is correctly handled, and it scopes the fix precisely to the reported str|None case rather than silently changing parsing semantics for other simple-type unions.

clusters.pick_reason: #3263 fixes cold-start refresh without changing any public interfaces: it adds an in-memory `eager_discovery_attempted` flag on `OAuthContext` and performs discovery before the refresh call, so it works for every existing `TokenStorage` implementation immediately. clusters.pick_reason: PR #3041's _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly locates the 'Bearer' scheme among segments and only collects auth-params up to the next scheme, correctly handling headers with multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic ..., Bearer ...'). PR #3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead takes everything after the first space in the whole header and splits it by top-level comma, which does not distinguish scheme boundaries and would merge params from a subsequent challenge into the same list in a multi-challenge header.
